title: quantization-personal-scratchpad-int8-fp8-bf16-breadcrumbs
content:
Quick timeline + breadcrumbs for the weird NaN/quality regression seen after INT8/FP8 experiments. Mostly personal notes - rough, incomplete, and a lot of trial-and-error history.

2024-11-18 10:15 - initial notes
- Experiment: quantize Llama-like 7B variant to INT8 using static PTQ pipeline (our qconfig). Observed occasional NaNs during decode in long-context (>2048) chat tests.
- Host: a100-40gb, CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 8.8, PyTorch 2.2, transformers 4.34, bitsandbytes 0.41
- Model: rw-llama-7b (fp16 baseline verified OK)
- Input distribution: synthetic long prompts ~4k tokens (chat history + user prompt)

Commands / env used (repro runs):
- export TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR=/tmp/torch_ext
- python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
- pip install -r requirements.txt (includes: torch==2.2.0+cu121, transformers, accelerate, bitsandbytes==0.41, giraffe-quantize==0.1.3)
- python scripts/quantize.py --model rw-llama-7b --dtype int8 --out-dir /tmp/qmodel_int8 --calib-samples 200
- python run_inference.py --model /tmp/qmodel_int8 --input tests/long_chat.json --max-len 4096 --batch 1

Observed error snippets (logs):
- RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered (during kernel launch in attention softmax)
- torch.nan encountered in attn_kv_cache (index 12345)
- Trace (excerpt):
  File "run_inference.py", line 212, in generate
    outputs = model.generate(inputs, max_new_tokens=512)
  File ".../quantize/wrapper.py", line 87, in forward
    attn_scores = scaled_qk.matmul(kv)
  File ".../aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Softmax.cu", line 44, in softmax_kernel
    // device side assert

Quick checks run
- Re-ran baseline fp16 model on same inputs -> no NaNs, output quality matches prior runs.
- Re-ran INT8 model with shorter contexts (<1024) -> no NaNs
- Re-ran INT8 with batch>1, same result: NaNs appear only with long context + streaming decode enabled

Hypotheses (brainstorm)
- Hypothesis A: KV cache accumulation in INT8 path suffers catastrophic quantization error causing extreme logits -> softmax overflow -> NaNs. Likely when sequence length grows and we repeatedly write/read cached keys/values with int8 quantization rounding.
- Hypothesis B: FP8 mixed representation (we tried FP8 intermediate) leading to reduced exponent range -> underflow/overflow in scaled dot-product at high sequence lengths.
- Hypothesis C: Kernel bug in custom fused attention implementation used for int8 path (indexing issue only hits with >2048 tokens).
- Hypothesis D: Calibration dataset for PTQ didn't cover long-range positional/interaction patterns -> scale factors too small for tails -> dynamic range blowup when encountering rare tokens/positions.

Commands tried to isolate:
1) Force cast KV cache to fp16 right before matmul (cheap hack)
- patch in wrapper: kv = kv.to(torch.float16) before attention matmul
- result: NaNs disappeared in a few runs (promising), but overall latency increased ~8% and some out-of-distribution prompts had degraded quality.

2) Recalculate scale factors using long context calibration set (synth long transcripts)
- re-run quantize.py with --calib-samples 2000 --include-long-context True
- result: reduced frequency of NaNs but not eliminated. Some failure modes remained.

3) Switch to per-channel scale (we were using per-tensor)
- modify quantizer config: per_channel=True for key/value projections
- result: dramatic reduction in NaNs on long context tests; slightly higher model size. Quality closer to fp16 baseline.

4) Try FP8 path (experimental)
- pip install fp8-lib==0.2; run quantize.py --dtype fp8
- result: immediate NaNs during calibration step on some layers (observed very small dynamic range). FP8 path seems brittle with our current kernels.

5) Try BF16 (training-aware quant)
- quantize.py --dtype bf16 (acted as cast-to-bf16 at inference)
- result: no NaNs, good quality, but memory savings minimal vs fp16 baseline. Good as a fallback for stability.

Repro recipe for the NaN (minimal):
- Use the INT8 quantized model with per-tensor scales, run decoder with streaming across long chat (>3k tokens). Repeat until NaN occurs (~1 in 10 runs depending on seed).
- Attach seed to reproduce: environment variable NUMPY_SEED=137 and SSEED=2081 (we saw correlation).

Additional logs / example offending output (redacted):
- Before crash: last logits sample (truncated) -> [12.3, 13.1, -nan, 0.01, -inf]
- Early indicators: sudden spike in max(logits) from ~15 to >1e9 between step 45 and 46; suggests scaling went wrong.

Notes about kernels + implementation details:
- Our int8 runtime uses a fused attention CUDA kernel (attention_fused.cu) that performs: quantize(q/k/v) -> store in kv cache -> dequantize on read? (implementation tries to avoid dequantize by doing matmul in int8 with int32 accumulation and then requantize). Complex path.
- Potential places for error: integer accumulation overflow not checked; bias/scale mismatches; index wrapping with >4096 offsets.

Next actionable experiments (todo list):
- [ ] Add assertions in fused kernel for max accumulation value (debug build) and produce counters to track overflow events.
- [ ] Implement a litmus test: create synthetic kv tensors with worst-case dynamic range (large differences) and run matmul in int8 pipeline to see overflow threshold.
- [ ] Re-run calibration with per-channel scales + long-context samples as default for k/v proj.
- [ ] Try hybrid: store kv in int8 but convert to fp16 in cache on read (we did a simple test with .to(fp16) and saw NaNs go away) - formalize as fallback for contexts > threshold length.
- [ ] Add more robust FP8 emulation (software fallback) to test exponent under/overflow boundaries.
- [ ] Audit indexing arithmetic in attention_fused.cu for 32-bit vs 64-bit counters - search for any %/mod ops that might overflow.

Quick wins found so far:
- Switching to per-channel quantization for k/v projections reduced NaN incidence dramatically. Seems most promising.
- BF16 as a safe fallback for production when stability is prioritized over memory.

Notes to product/ops (copy for email later):
- If customers on dedicated capacity request INT8, warn that long-context workloads may see rare NaNs with current default per-tensor PTQ. Recommend per-channel quantization or BF16 fallback for high-context apps.

Unresolved questions / open investigations:
- Why does streaming decode exacerbate the problem compared to batched offline decode? (Is it due to repeated writes to same cache memory exposing a bug?)
- Are specific tokens/positions more likely to trigger overflow (rare tokens with extreme embeddings)? Need to search failure prompts for token frequency anomalies.
- Is there any correlation with specific kernel launch parameters (threads per block) that change with batch/seq length?

Experiment logs (shorthands)
- Run A: INT8 per-tensor (baseline) -> NaN freq ~10% on long chat
- Run B: INT8 per-channel -> NaN freq ~0.3%
- Run C: INT8 per-tensor + on-read cast to fp16 -> NaN freq ~0.1% but +8% latency
- Run D: FP8 (experimental) -> unstable during calibration -> blocked
- Run E: BF16 -> stable, quality OK, no NaNs

Tags for myself: TODO: instrument kernels, add unit tests for accumulation overflow, expand calibration corpora, consider runtime thresholds (if seq_len > 2048 then use per-channel or bf16).

Reference notes:
- Related internal doc: confluence:/ML/quantization/long-context-issues (link above)
- Prior incident: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad-int8-fp8-bf16-maya.json (see similar notes, earlier run Nov 2024)

Last quick thought: it looked like the worst-case blowup always happens after the model emits a long sequence of punctuation/newline tokens in the prompt (many repeated token ids). That could interact badly with scale estimation if calibration didn't see long repeated-token runs. Add synthetic calibration samples with repeated-sequence patterns.

-- Maya

(End of scratchpad)
